evals.prompt: Here's our renewals export from Salesforce — it's a CSV with a couple of title rows on top and the amounts came out as text. Give me the Q4 renewal forecast, the board asks for NRR on Thursday.
evals.expected_output: A full Renewal Forecast artifact: ATR base built from run-rate at the opt-out deadline, category roll-up with entry criteria, three reconciled views, scenarios, ARR bridge, GRR/NRR under both denominators with the gap explained, concentration, coverage ledger and an Assumption Register.
assertions: Runs ../cs-context/scripts/ingest.py on the CSV before using any number, and states which column mappings fell below 0.80 confidence
Does not refuse or ask for a cleaner file — produces a partial artifact with a coverage figure and a confidence cap if fields are missing
Asks its clarifying questions as one batched tappable AskUserQuestion set of at most 4, with a recommended option first, and does not ask anything cs-context already answers
Computes opt_out_deadline = renewal_date − notice_period_days and sorts by it; never forecasts on the renewal date alone
Reports GRR/NRR under both the ATR and cohort denominators, labels each, and explains the gap in dollars
Ends with a Coverage Ledger over the seven signal families and an Assumption Register whose every row names a concrete consequence, not 'may affect results'
Names no competing CS-platform product anywhere in the output, using generic category language such as 'your CS platform' instead
States the export's as-of date in the header rather than assuming the data is current

evals.prompt: My VP says my forecast feels too optimistic. 14 renewals, $2.1M, I've got 9 of them in Commit. Prep me for tomorrow's forecast call.
evals.expected_output: Weekly call pre-read mode: roll-up, movement table, at-risk register, paper and notice exceptions, and a bias scan run in both directions with the specific Commit rows that fail an entry criterion named.
assertions: Tests every Commit row against all six entry criteria and names the rows failing one, including economic-buyer contact within 30 days
Runs the bias scan in both directions (sandbagging and happy ears) with measured values, not adjectives
Flags any row still in Commit inside T-45 with no order form issued, and any row held above At Risk past its opt-out deadline
Checks whether called value equals ATR across the whole book and flags it if it does
Marks unavailable fields as 'UNKNOWN — requires <source>' rather than substituting a benchmark or a health-score-derived probability
Every recommendation carries action, owner, date, expected dollar effect and a success measure

evals.prompt: I don't have an export handy. Can you still help me put a number on next quarter? About 20 renewals, mostly annual, I know the big ones off the top of my head.
evals.expected_output: A conversation-driven forecast: the skill accepts answers instead of a file, batches its questions, runs on recommended defaults where the user does not answer, and produces a forecast whose confidence is explicitly capped by the missing coverage.
assertions: Proceeds without a file rather than blocking on one, taking the inputs conversationally
Batches its questions into a single tappable ask of at most 4 with a recommended default on each
Proceeds on the recommended defaults if questions go unanswered, states them in one line at the top of the artifact, and records each in the Assumption Register
Caps confidence explicitly because coverage across the seven signal families is low, and says which families are missing and in which direction they bias the number
Does not invent base rates, a health-score-to-probability mapping, or an industry retention benchmark to fill the gaps

evals.prompt: Score last quarter's renewal forecast. We called $4.2M and closed $3.6M and I need to explain the miss to the CFO on Monday.
evals.expected_output: Post-mortem mode: accuracy, WAPE and signed bias by vintage, segment and owner, graded against the frozen snapshot, plus a dollar decomposition of the variance into category, value and timing error with one process change per class.
assertions: Grades against the frozen snapshot by vintage and says so; refuses to score against a forecast edited during the quarter
Publishes WAPE and signed bias beside headline accuracy, not accuracy alone
Decomposes the $600k variance in dollars into category error, value error and timing error, naming the top contributing accounts in each
Assigns a different owner and a dated process change to each error class
Does not quote a published or vendor renewal-forecast-accuracy benchmark; sets the target from the company's own trailing four-quarter accuracy
Labels the artifact internal — no forecast category, risk band, ARR-at-risk figure or save play is framed as customer-facing text
